info.bio:
Joseph Vernon Turner Jr, conocido como Big Joe Turner (Kansas City,18 de mayo de 1911 - Inglewood, 24 de noviembre de 1985) fue un cantante de blues y pionero del rock and roll estadounidense.

Su carrera comienza a principios de los años 1930 dentro de la influencia del jazz de Kansas para evolucionar al boogie-woogie al final de esa década en Nueva York. En los años 50 alcanzaría su mayor fama con las primeras grabaciones de rock and roll, destacando su tema "Shake, Rattle and Roll".

scenes.desc: En Estados Unidos la crítica, que detesta a Black Sabbath y a Judas Priest, evita el término «heavy metal» y prefiere «hard rock», el formato radiofónico de moda en los setenta, donde caben grupos muy populares que no cumplen del todo el código: Aerosmith (1973) y Kiss (1974) son demasiado melódicos para ser heavy en esa década. Cuando el género se fragmente, el lite metal adoptará su estilo vocal melódico y sus armonías, y ambos acabarán dentro del metal ampliado. Alice Cooper, que compartía cartel con Black Sabbath, regala al heavy la estética visual de película de terror.

podcast.title: Audience Crossover with Louis Jordan
podcast.body: Big Joe Turner's audience was part of the crossover demographic that also listened to Louis Jordan's music. "just as much as you were to the audience that was listening to Big Joe Turner"

podcast.title: Blues Club Patronage
podcast.body: As a child, Jerry Lee Lewis would regularly sneak into a local blues club with an entirely Black clientele to watch performers like Big Joe Turner, Fats Domino, Charles Brown, and BB King until he was kicked out by the owner in the segregated South. "he would regularly sneak into a local blues club with an otherwise entirely black-cli-on-tail and hide under the table to watch people like Fat Stummino, Charles Brown, BB King, and Big Joe Turner."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Blues Shout-Out Style
podcast.body: Big Joe Turner was a prominent blues shout-out, a type of singer, usually a man, who could sing loudly and powerfully enough to be heard over a band without amplification in the early 20th century. Even with the introduction of unreliable microphones and weak amplification, shout-outs like Turner could compete with the volume of big bands like Count Basie's by sheer vocal force. "Blues shelters like Big Joe Turner could compete with that power, and get excited by the sheer volume of their voice, even over bands like Count Basis."

podcast.title: Blues Shouter Influence
podcast.body: Big Joe Turner was cited as a significant inspiration for Wynonie Harris's primary vocal style as a blues shouter. "inspired by people like Big Joe Turner and Jimmy Rushing."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Characterized by Misogyny in Work
podcast.body: Much of Big Joe Turner's work, including his original version of "Honey Hush," was characterized by misogynistic themes. "It's not one of Turner's best to be honest, leaning too heavily on the misogyny that characterized too much of his work."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 44: "Train Kept A-Rollin'", by Johnny Burnette and the Rock 'n' Roll Trio

podcast.title: Late Career Recordings
podcast.body: Big Joe Turner was among the artists whose late-career recordings were released by Johnny Otis's Blues Spectrum Records in the 1970s. Some of these recordings were Turner's last ever. "He ran blues spectrum records in the 70s, which put out late career recordings by people like Charles Brown, Big Joe Turner and Louis Jordan. Some of them their last ever recordings"

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: REUPLOAD Episode 71: "Willie and the Hand Jive" by Johnny Otis

podcast.title: Male Jump Band Artist Typically Covered by Country Musicians
podcast.body: Big Joe Turner is cited as an example of a male jump band artist whose R&B music was more typically performed by country musicians exploring R&B, differentiating from Janice Martin's choice of female R&B singers with a jazzier sound. "performing music originally recorded by male jump band artists like Louis Jordan or Big Joe Turner."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 40: "Drugstore Rock 'n' Roll" by Janis Martin

podcast.title: Transition to Star Singer
podcast.body: After the Musicians' Union Strike of 1942-44, the tradition of instrumentalists being the stars in American music ended, giving way to singers. Joe Turner, alongside Frank Sinatra, became one of these new singing stars, solidifying his role in the emerging rhythm and blues genre. "Instead, they were singers, like Frank Sinatra, and like Joe Turner."
